subject: Re: Runtime sidecar subprocessor mapping and telemetry access - clarification
messages:
From: Erin Patel <erin@healthgrid.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medworks.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runtime sidecar - list of subprocessors + telemetry question

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our SIG/CAIQ review for the integration, InfoSec has a couple of follow-ups specifically about the runtime sidecar that ships with Redwood’s private deployment:

1) Can you provide a CSV mapping of all subprocessors involved in the sidecar (agents, metrics, log-forwarders, CDN endpoints) including vendor name, purpose, data residency, and whether the vendor has access to customer telemetry or encryption keys?

2) Does the sidecar emit any telemetry that is sent to third parties (hostnames, full request paths, unhashed identifiers)? If so, we need retention windows and an assurance about PII exclusion.

3) Any architecture/network diagram that shows egress flows from the sidecar to external vendors would be helpful for our network team.

Can you send these by Mon Jun 23 so we can keep the SIG response on schedule? If anything is sensitive, a redacted inventory is fine but please flag which items will need an NDA or redaction.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if that’s easier.

Best,
Erin
Erin Patel
Security Manager, HealthGrid
 erin@healthgrid.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Erin Patel <erin@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medworks.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime sidecar - list of subprocessors + telemetry question

Erin,

Thanks — we can absolutely supply that. I’ve attached an initial subprocessor CSV and a network diagram that shows common egress paths for the sidecar (attached: subprocessor_inventory_20250619.csv, runtime_sidecar_network_diagram.pdf). A couple of quick summary points up front to save time:

- Telemetry scope: the sidecar emits aggregated metrics (prometheus-style counters and histograms) and structured logs. No full request bodies or raw PII are sent by default. Identifiers are hashed at source (salted, ephemeral) unless the customer specifically configures debug-mode.
- Subprocessor access: metrics storage and log forwarding are handled by third-party vendors noted in the CSV (MetricsCo, LogForward Inc., CDNHub). None of these vendors have access to unencrypted customer data or customer-managed KMS keys.
- Retention: telemetry aggregates retained for 30 days by default; raw logs (if enabled) are retained per customer config and can be set to 0/7/30/90 days.

If you can confirm the SIG section you’re working on (SIG-Lite vs full SIG), we’ll prepare the corresponding evidence bundle. For SIG-Lite we can provide the CSV + diagram and a short attestation; for full SIG we’ll need to include control narratives and some artifacts (SOC 2 section references, encryption key path docs).

I’m copying my cloud security lead (Jonas) and compliance ops (Marissa) to help with the detailed mapping and to prepare SIG responses. Expect a follow-up from us with clarified vendor-level telemetry statements by Mon.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Manager, Compliance & Trust Operations
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACTION: Sidecar vendor telemetry & SIG-Lite artifacts (MedWorks ask)

Rachel / Marissa —

Quick status and vendor mapping (attached: sig-lite-responses-asked.xlsx):

- MetricsCo (metrics-hosting.example.com): receives aggregated metrics (counters/histograms). Identifiers are hashed with an ephemeral salt at the sidecar; no unhashed user identifiers are transmitted. Retention: 30 days. No KMS access.
- LogForward Inc (logs.redwood-logs.example.net): receives structured logs when customer enables log-forwarding. By default logs exclude request bodies and PII; customers can enable debug-logs (explicit config) which will be marked as "debug-mode" and require customer confirmation. Default retention 30 days; configurable. LogForward does not have access to customer-managed KMS keys.
- CDNHub (cdnhub.example.com): used for static asset distribution and update manifests. No telemetry access to request-level payloads beyond standard HTTP headers. Retention not applicable.
- AuthStore (authstore.example.com): token revocation and session checks; handles hashed session ids only, no plaintext credentials. AuthStore is a subcontractor of our Auth provider; we list them as a transitive subprocessor in the CSV.

Notes:
- No external vendor has access to unencrypted customer data or to our customer-managed KMS. We use envelope encryption; customer-managed keys stay in the customer's KMS except in Dedicated environments where keys may be provisioned into HSM partitions we control (documented in KMS keyflow link).
- Telemetry sent to vendors is limited by default; only customers who enable additional debug/diagnostic flags will send more verbose telemetry. We will mark those rows in the CSV as "configurable/opt-in".

Next steps: I attached the SIG-Lite draft with vendor-level control statements filled. Rachel — if this looks good I can redact vendor billing IDs and submit the bundle to Erin by EOD Mon.

-- Jonas
Jonas Weber
Cloud Security Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
